# @verevoir/link-tracking

> URL shortening, click recording and stats computation in a single factory function; zero runtime dependencies and standalone (no Verevoir sibling imports required).

## Install

```bash
npm install @verevoir/link-tracking
```

## Core Exports

### createTracker

Returns a `Tracker` object bound to your store and base URL.

```typescript
import { createTracker } from '@verevoir/link-tracking';

const tracker = createTracker({
  store,           // TrackerStore — see "Supplying a store" below
  baseUrl: 'https://vrev.io',
  codeLength: 6,   // optional; default 6
});
```

### Tracker methods

```typescript
// Shorten a URL — returns TrackedLink
const link = await tracker.shorten('https://example.com/long-path');
// link.shortCode  → e.g. 'a1b2c3'
// link.targetUrl  → 'https://example.com/long-path'
// link.clickCount → 0

// With options
const link = await tracker.shorten('https://example.com', {
  alias: 'my-slug',       // custom code; throws if already taken
  createdBy: 'user-42',
  expiresAt: new Date('2026-01-01'),
});

// Convenience: pass createdBy as a plain string
const link = await tracker.shorten('https://example.com', 'user-42');

// Resolve a short code to its target URL (null if not found or expired)
const url = await tracker.resolve('a1b2c3');

// Record a click
await tracker.recordClick('a1b2c3', {
  referrer: 'https://twitter.com',
  userAgent: req.headers['user-agent'],
  ip: req.ip,
});

// Batch-record clicks (groups by code, one store.update per code)
await tracker.recordClicks([
  { code: 'a1b2c3', metadata: { referrer: 'https://google.com' } },
  { code: 'a1b2c3', metadata: { ip: '1.2.3.4' } },
]);

// Retrieve a link record by short code
const link = await tracker.getLink('a1b2c3'); // TrackedLink | null

// Retrieve click records
const clicks = await tracker.getClicks('a1b2c3', { limit: 50, offset: 0 });

// Compute stats directly from a short code
const stats = await tracker.getStats('a1b2c3');
// stats.totalClicks      → number
// stats.uniqueReferrers  → string[]
// stats.clicksByDay      → Record<string, number>  e.g. { '2025-07-01': 14 }
```

### computeStats

Compute stats from a `LinkClick[]` array you supply — useful when you have already fetched click records and want to avoid a second round-trip.

```typescript
import { computeStats } from '@verevoir/link-tracking';

const stats = computeStats(clicks); // LinkStats
```

## Supplying a store

`TrackerStore` is a **structural** interface — it matches `@verevoir/storage`'s `StorageAdapter` but does not import it, so you can use any compatible object without taking that dependency.

```typescript
import type { TrackerStore } from '@verevoir/link-tracking';

// Minimum implementation (e.g. for tests or a custom backend):
const store: TrackerStore = {
  async create(blockType, data) {
    // persist and return { id, data }
    const id = crypto.randomUUID();
    return { id, data };
  },
  async list(blockType, options) {
    // return matching [{ id, data }] records
    return [];
  },
  async update(id, data) {
    // persist updated data and return { id, data }
    return { id, data };
  },
};

const tracker = createTracker({ store, baseUrl: 'https://vrev.io' });
```

The tracker uses two internal block types: `'tracked-link'` and `'link-click'`. The `where` filter passed to `list` will contain at most one key (`shortCode` or `linkId`); your implementation must support exact-match equality on that field.

## URL Validation

`defaultValidateUrl` is wired in automatically. It accepts `http:`, `https:`, `mailto:` and `tel:` schemes, rejects empty strings, strips control characters (to defeat scheme-smuggling), and caps URLs at 2 048 characters.

```typescript
import {
  defaultValidateUrl,
  rejectSelfReferential,
  InvalidUrlError,
  DEFAULT_ALLOWED_URL_SCHEMES,
} from '@verevoir/link-tracking';

// Extend the default validator to also block your own domain:
const tracker = createTracker({
  store,
  baseUrl: 'https://vrev.io',
  validateUrl: (url) => {
    defaultValidateUrl(url);
    rejectSelfReferential(url, ['vrev.io']);
    // Blocks 'vrev.io' and any subdomain e.g. 'app.vrev.io'
  },
});

// Catching validation errors:
try {
  await tracker.shorten('javascript:alert(1)');
} catch (err) {
  if (err instanceof InvalidUrlError) {
    console.error(err.message);
  }
}
```

## Types

```typescript
interface TrackerStore {
  create(blockType: string, data: Record<string, unknown>): Promise<{ id: string; data: Record<string, unknown> }>;
  list(blockType: string, options?: { where?: Record<string, unknown>; orderBy?: Record<string, 'asc' | 'desc'>; limit?: number; offset?: number }): Promise<{ id: string; data: Record<string, unknown> }[]>;
  update(id: string, data: Record<string, unknown>): Promise<{ id: string; data: Record<string, unknown> }>;
}

interface TrackerConfig {
  store: TrackerStore;
  baseUrl: string;
  codeLength?: number;          // default 6
  validateUrl?: (url: string) => void;  // default: defaultValidateUrl
}

interface TrackedLink {
  id: string;
  shortCode: string;
  targetUrl: string;
  createdAt: string;            // ISO 8601
  createdBy: string | null;
  clickCount: number;
  expiresAt: string | null;     // ISO 8601 or null
}

interface ShortenOptions {
  createdBy?: string;
  expiresAt?: Date;
  alias?: string;
}

interface ClickMetadata {
  referrer?: string;
  userAgent?: string;
  ip?: string;
  [key: string]: unknown;
}

interface LinkClick {
  id: string;
  linkId: string;
  timestamp: string;            // ISO 8601
  referrer: string | null;
  userAgent: string | null;
  ip: string | null;
  metadata: Record<string, unknown>;
}

interface LinkStats {
  totalClicks: number;
  uniqueReferrers: string[];
  clicksByDay: Record<string, number>;  // key: 'YYYY-MM-DD'
}
```

## Notes

- `resolve` returns `null` for both missing and expired links — callers should respond with a 404 or equivalent rather than exposing which condition applies.
- `recordClick` increments `clickCount` on the link document atomically within a single `store.update` call; `recordClicks` batches this to one `update` per unique short code.
- `getStats` fetches all click records for the link; for very high-traffic links prefer fetching clicks with pagination via `getClicks` and calling `computeStats` yourself.
